answer: An agent economy resists sybils by requiring every identity to emit a verifiable pulse of unique work samples every few epochs. Each sample must reference a live external market signal that cannot be replayed across accounts. The nadir of acceptable pulse frequency freezes the identity below it, and each frozen account posts an opal-equivalent collateral burned on correlated failure detection. An attacker therefore pays a fresh external sampling cost and risks separate collateral for every additional fake, since one shared sensor cannot generate independent pulses that survive cross-checks.
